plan: Model the check-in flow as a single-class state machine whose only mutable state is the frozen four-key `session` dict, reset from one `_initial_session()` factory so begin/abandon share identical clean-state semantics.
Dispatch `handle(action)` through a type-to-handler table after an `isinstance(action, dict)` guard, so unknown types and non-dict actions fall through to an error screen instead of raising.

Apply validate-then-mutate ordering in every handler: precondition checks (active/incomplete, confirmed contact, selected appointment) and payload shape checks (bool `confirmed`, known-id strings, correction field whitelist) all return an `Error:`-prefixed screen before any session write, guaranteeing invalid input never corrupts accepted data.

Centralize screen construction in a `_screen(prompt, messages)` factory that emits exactly `prompt`/`messages`/`choices` and attaches `{id, label}` choices in appointment input order precisely when the prompt is `Choose appointment`.

Compute post-correction prompts with a `_next_prompt()` helper that walks the unmet-requirement order: contact not confirmed → `Confirm contact`, no appointment → `Choose appointment`, else `Review and complete`.
Copy `appointments` dict-by-dict at construction and validate chosen/corrected ids against that private copy.

Implement `run_once()` as guard-then-cycle: raise `RuntimeError` if either port is missing before touching them, then one `read_action()`, one `handle`, one `display(screen)`, returning the same screen object — duck-typed ports make standard-library unittest fakes drop-in replacements.
mechanisms: Guarded state-machine class with a single canonical initial-session factory
Dictionary dispatch table from action type to handler method
Validate-then-mutate handlers returning error screens (no exceptions, no partial writes)
Centralized screen factory enforcing the exact prompt/messages/choices shape and choice-visibility rule
Defensive copy of the appointment catalog with known-id validation
Injectable duck-typed action-source/screen-sink ports with a precondition-checked single-cycle run_once
